findings.claim: The spec names three environmental challenges: deforestation, increased carbon dioxide levels leading to potential global warming, and the need for fair trade.
findings.truth: Spec 3.3.2 is headed 'Environmental, social and economic challenge'. Deforestation and carbon dioxide are environmental; the need for fair trade is a social and economic challenge, not an environmental one. Repeated in the revision tip, the conclusion, practice question 1, knowledge check 1 and flashcard 1.

findings.claim: Fair trade ensures that producers in developing countries receive fair payment and work in safe conditions.
findings.truth: Fairtrade's own wording is aspirational: it sets a Minimum Price as 'a safety net' and works so farmers can 'earn a decent income, work in safe conditions'. It does not claim to ensure or guarantee this. Repeated in knowledge check 3 and practice question 5.

findings.claim: FSC certification means the timber comes from sustainably managed forests where trees are replanted at the same rate they are harvested.
findings.truth: FSC certification means the wood comes from environmentally, socially and economically responsible sources, judged against 10 principles covering ecosystems, workers and indigenous rights. It is not defined by a replanting rate.

findings.claim: Sustainably managed forests: forests managed so that trees are replanted at the same rate they are harvested (glossary term and the matching data-def).
findings.truth: A tight but standard GCSE definition of sustainable forestry. Left as taught; the FSC claim in F3 is the one that misattributes it to a certification scheme.

findings.claim: William Morris ... championed traditional craftsmanship and founded the Arts and Crafts movement.
findings.truth: Morris did not found the movement. It was inspired by Carlyle, Ruskin and Morris, and the term 'Arts and Crafts' was coined by T. J. Cobden-Sanderson at the Arts and Crafts Exhibition Society in 1887. Morris was its main influence and leading figure. Also in glossary_terms[0].
findings.evidence: Wikipedia, Arts and Crafts movement and William Morris, fetched 2026-09-18

findings.claim: Morris's philosophy that “nothing should be in your houses that you do not know to be useful or believe to be beautiful”
findings.truth: The wording is “Have nothing in your houses that you do not know to be useful, or believe to be beautiful.” (The Beauty of Life, lecture to the Birmingham Society of Arts, 19 February 1880).

findings.claim: You must study at least one category in depth for your NEA.
findings.truth: Spec 3.3.6 requires in-depth knowledge of one material category across the selection of materials to specialist techniques sections. That content is examined in the written paper as well as used in the NEA, so tying it to the NEA alone understates what is examined.
findings.evidence: spec 3.3.6 and 2.2 Assessments (Paper 1 Section C, 50 marks)

findings.claim: the specification lists six material categories that designers work with.
findings.truth: The sentence starts with a lower-case word, left by an earlier sweep that replaced a board name.

findings.claim: His Louis Ghost Chair (2002), made from transparent polycarbonate
findings.truth: Sources disagree on the date: Wikipedia's Philippe Starck article gives 2000, while Kartell and most design references give 2002. The material, the maker and the 18th-century Louis reference are all correct. Not corrected because the true value is not settled.
findings.evidence: Wikipedia, Philippe Starck, fetched 2026-09-18; Kartell page unreachable

findings.claim: list the five design strategies named in The spec from memory
findings.truth: Stray capital left by an earlier sweep that replaced a board name.

findings.claim: write down the three evaluation skills The spec expects you to demonstrate
findings.truth: Stray capital left by an earlier sweep that replaced a board name.

findings.claim: the specification uses the example of ±2 mm for general workshop tolerances.
findings.truth: The sentence starts with a lower-case word. The ±2 mm figure itself is the spec's own worked example and is correct.

findings.claim: 'State the three factors a designer should consider when selecting materials for a prototype.' labelled 2 marks, mark scheme ends 'Any two for 2 marks.'
findings.truth: The question asks for three but only two are credited. The question now asks for two, matching the mark label and the scheme.
findings.evidence: the question's own mark scheme; spec 3.3.7

findings.claim: CNC — Computer Numerical Control — a subtractive process where a computer-controlled tool cuts material from a solid block.
findings.truth: CNC is the automated control of machine tools by a computer. It drives additive machines too — 3D printers also run on G-code — so it is not itself a subtractive process. The lesson body already treats CNC routing and milling correctly as wastage.

findings.claim: Injection moulding requires an expensive steel mould ... For 500 units, injection moulding is more cost-effective overall.
findings.truth: Injection moulds are made from aluminium as well as steel, and at 500 units the cheaper route depends on the tooling cost against the batch value. A 6-mark discussion should credit either conclusion when the cost reasoning is sound.
findings.evidence: recomputation of the cost argument; spec 3.3.11

findings.claim: In Section C of the AQA exam, you may be asked to explain why a designer would use a particular research method.
findings.truth: House rule: the board is never named in student-facing text. The section is now described ('the designing and making section of the written exam'), which is the correct section for this unit.
findings.evidence: spec 2.2 Assessments (Section C, designing and making principles, 50 marks)

findings.truth: House rule: the board is never named in student-facing text. Replaced with 'the specification' / 'the design and technology specification'. The shortened description is 90 characters.

findings.truth: Students see the placeholder caption under the diagram. Out of scope for a fact-check edit, but it needs a caption pass on lessons 5 and 6.

findings.truth: British spelling is 'ageing'. Not corrected because the change is inaudible and would re-narrate three clips for nothing.

summary: Seven lessons checked against the spec and against Wikipedia, Fairtrade and FSC for every designer, company and technical claim. Every named designer and company is on the spec list and every date, product and answer key checks out; the substantive errors are fair trade taught as an environmental challenge, a misquoted and mis-credited William Morris, CNC defined as a subtractive process, an unsupported injection-moulding verdict, a 3-for-2-marks question, and the board named in seventeen student-facing places.
